summary.text: One of Penelope's suitors in Apollodorus' catalogue of the fifty-seven wooers from Dulichium — distinct from the suitor of the same name from Zacynthus in Epitome 7.29, and a namesake of the Phoenician king and of the Trojan who faced Achilles at the Scaean gate.

story.text: Apollodorus names Agenor among the suitors who devoured Odysseus' substance, listed after Clytius and before Eurypylus in the long company of Penelope's wooers.
The same name appears again among the wooers from Zacynthus in Epitome 7.29 — a different suitor.
